Jordan: Weekly train update 12: planned model switchover to v3.7-opt (quantized) starting 04:00 UTC. Heads-up: this touches serving kernels + fallback routing.
Ivy: Canary started at 04:05 UTC. Short regression on our eval suite for conversational quality (BLEU/Rouge drop ~1.8–2.4%). No customer errors, but QA flagged reduced fidelity on a prompt subset.
Marco: Reproduced locally. The quant profile for long-context seems to underweight attention precision for certain token types. Rolling back model on canary and pausing train.
Marco: Rollback command:
```
svcctl deploy --env canary --model-id v3.7 --force-revert
```
sre-bot: [04:18 UTC] Canary revert completed: 2/2 pods back to v3.7 stable. Telemetry: CPU/GPU and latency within normal bounds. (link: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/1357)
Ivy: After revert, evals returned to baseline within one run. QA: will run expanded prompt sweep and post a readout in ~30m.
Jordan: Because this is a model-quality regression, instituting a temporary release freeze for the entire train: 04:3010:30 UTC. No model or routing changes during freeze. If you need an exemption include: impact statement, test plan, and rollback plan.
QA-Alex: Will post the full eval artifact (notebook + metrics) to PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/qa/model-evals/210. Key failing prompts attached there.
Marco: Next steps: (1) investigate quant profile adjustments, (2) add targeted unit tests for attention precision edgecases, (3) re-run canary with smaller bin-width + reduced concurrency.
Jordan: Ops note: when we resume, well enable canary-only traffic at 2% for 2h, then step to 10% if stable. Documented in rollout playbook.
Ivy: Thanks all 12 please keep updates in this thread and tag @oncall for any customer anomalies. :memo:
